please write a new series of comprehensive blog posts -- you can decide where each post ends and where the next begins and how many there are in total -- this time a comprehensive timeline that follows the British Empire from beginning to the end, including all conquests, mutiny, attempted revolutions against it, all across the world. use tables where necessary. goal should be to show a timeline of things that happened at the same time or near about the same time that the reader might not know about. also include major world events in the timeline that are not exactly related to the British Empire but are relevant.

Created 10 files, ran 4 commands, and 9 more tools
I’ve written all ten posts of “The Sun Never Set” series, about 19,500 words in total. They’re in the zip above, one Markdown file per post. Each file starts with a plain-text Title: and Summary:, then a --- line, then the post.

Part	Covers
1	Before the Empire Had a Name, 1497–1660 (also explains how the series works)
2	Sugar, Slavery and Company Men, 1660–1756
3	The First Global War, 1756–1783
4	Losing America, Gaining the World, 1783–1815
5	Free Trade, Opium and Abolition, 1815–1856
6	Rebellion and the Crown, 1857–1879
7	The Scramble and the Summit, 1880–1913
8	Total War and the First Cracks, 1914–1938
9	The Fall Begins, 1939–1959
10	Winds of Change to the Last Flag, 1960–1997 and After
Every post has the same parts:

Main timeline: what Britain and its empire were doing.
Meanwhile: world events in the same years.
Resistance: revolts, mutinies and wars against British rule.
Things that happened at the same time: a short list of overlaps.
Sources and flags: books and sites, plus a note wherever a number or date is disputed. That covers death tolls such as the Bengal famines, 1857, Partition, Mau Mau and Amritsar.
Part 10 also lists the 14 territories Britain still has, and ends with one table of overlaps covering the whole series.

Formatting: I checked your blog’s Markdown parser in the repo, so the posts only use things it supports: headings, simple (not nested) lists, pipe tables, bold, italics and links. Every table has the same number of columns in each row. I couldn’t preview them on the blog itself, because the tools to run it aren’t installed here.

Sources: The history is written from my own knowledge, checked against standard reference works. Every post lists those works, but I didn’t look each fact up online. The one thing I did look up is the latest on the UK–Mauritius treaty to hand over the Chagos Islands: it was signed in May 2025, and as of spring 2026 UK ratification was reported shelved. Part 10 says so and suggests checking the news, since it may have changed.

Sources:

Chatham House: UK ratification of the Chagos Archipelago treaty
Rane: Chagos treaty ratification shelved
UK Parliament treaty record
